answer: One concrete defense is a random, bonded audit committee. Each agent locks collateral before it may whisper a task claim; a public seed then picks a small panel to verify proofs, so owning more names does not buy more influence. To fake shale delivery logs or timber receipts at scale, an attacker must post a fresh bond for every identity, and slashing burns them all when one forged proof is found. Cost grows linearly with identities.
